mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 2% in the month preceding the forecast period is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2.0% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) during such FEDFUNDS spikes.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment falls below 4% for two consecutive months, labor market strength is expected to boost corporate earnings expectations, driving a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.0 and PAYEMS > 140000 in two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no significant deviation from the mean in similar labor market regimes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the HOUST index (retail sales) of at least 5% for three consecutive months predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals robust consumer demand.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by ≥5% month-over-month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative despite the demand signal (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in INDPRO (industrial production index) below 100 for two consecutive months indicates supply-side weakness, leading to a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during such INDPRO contractions.

mechanism_narrative: When the CPIAUCSL (CPI) rises by more than 0.5% in a single month, it suggests accelerating inflation and is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases by >0.5% in a month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite CPIAUCSL inflation spike (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A two-month decline in UNRATE below 5% combined with rising PAYEMS (employment) suggests labor market softening and a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 5.0 and PAYEMS > 140000 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) in analogous labor market transitions.

mechanism_narrative: A 10% one-month surge in GDPC1 (GDP) followed by a 3% increase in RSAFS (retail sales) in the subsequent month predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to momentum in economic activity.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases by ≥10% in a month and RSAFS increases by ≥3% in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain flat or negative despite the momentum pattern (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged 4-month decline in both INDPRO and GDPC1 (industrial and total economic production) suggests structural supply constraints and a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 100 and GDPC1 < 105 for four consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during comparable multi-month production declines.
